title: Migrate Monolith to Microservices
question: Migrate legacy monolithic application to microservices. Requirements: 1) Monolith has 500K lines of code, 2) Critical business application with 24/7 uptime requirement, 3) Cannot stop business during migration, 4) Database is tightly coupled, 5) Team has limited microservices experience, 6) Need to show business value incrementally. Discuss: starting with domain analysis to identify bounded contexts and business capabilities, using Domain-Driven Design to define service boundaries, applying strangler fig pattern to gradually replace monolith functionality, identifying seams in monolith (modules with clear boundaries), starting with leaf services (services with no dependencies on other parts), extracting services that change frequently or have different scaling needs, implementing API gateway to route requests to monolith or microservices transparently, using feature flags to switch between old and new implementation, implementing anti-corruption layer to translate between monolith and microservices, handling database decomposition with database-per-service pattern, using database views or CDC (Change Data Capture) for shared data during transition, implementing event-driven communication between services, using saga pattern for distributed transactions, extracting services in priority order (high business value, low risk first), implementing comprehensive testing (contract testing, integration testing), using parallel runs to verify new services match monolith behavior, implementing monitoring and observability (distributed tracing, centralized logging), migrating data gradually (dual writes, eventual consistency), and building team expertise through training and starting with non-critical services.

title: Design Scalable Social Media Platform
question: Design architecture for social media platform. Requirements: 1) 10M users, 2) Users post content (text, images, videos), 3) Follow other users and see their posts in feed, 4) Like, comment, share posts, 5) Real-time notifications, 6) Search functionality, 7) High availability and performance. Discuss: using microservices architecture with services: User Service (profiles, authentication), Post Service (create, read posts), Feed Service (generate user feeds), Notification Service (push notifications), Search Service (full-text search), Media Service (upload, process, serve media), using API Gateway for routing and rate limiting, implementing user authentication with JWT tokens, using CDN for serving static content and media files, storing media files in object storage (S3) with transcoding pipeline for videos, using separate write and read databases (CQRS pattern), storing posts in primary database (PostgreSQL for consistency), denormalizing feed data in NoSQL (Cassandra) for fast reads, implementing fan-out on write approach for feeds (pre-compute feeds when post is created), using Redis cache for hot data (user sessions, recent posts, trending content), implementing pagination and infinite scroll for feeds, using Kafka for event streaming (post created, user followed), consuming events to update feeds and send notifications, implementing notification service with WebSockets for real-time updates and Firebase/SNS for mobile push, using Elasticsearch for full-text search with async indexing, implementing rate limiting per user to prevent abuse, using database sharding by user ID for horizontal scaling, implementing image processing pipeline (resize, compress, generate thumbnails), using load balancers for distributing traffic, implementing circuit breakers and bulkheads for resilience, using monitoring and alerting (Prometheus, Grafana), and implementing data analytics pipeline for insights.

title: Multi-Region High Availability System
question: Design multi-region deployment for global application. Requirements: 1) Users across Americas, Europe, Asia, 2) Low latency for all regions, 3) 99.99% availability, 4) Data sovereignty compliance (GDPR, data residency), 5) Disaster recovery, 6) Cost optimization. Discuss: deploying application in multiple AWS/Azure regions (US-East, EU-West, Asia-Pacific), using Route 53/Traffic Manager for global load balancing with latency-based routing, implementing active-active deployment where all regions serve traffic, using CDN (CloudFront, Akadam) for static content delivery, implementing database replication across regions: multi-master for high availability or master-slave with read replicas, using database routing based on user location, implementing data residency by storing EU user data in EU region to comply with GDPR, using data partitioning by geography, implementing cross-region data sync with conflict resolution for global data, using event-driven architecture with Kafka/Kinesis for cross-region event propagation, implementing disaster recovery with automatic failover, using health checks to detect region failures and route traffic to healthy regions, implementing data backup strategy with cross-region backup replication, using infrastructure as code (Terraform, CloudFormation) for multi-region deployment, implementing centralized monitoring across regions with aggregated dashboards, using distributed tracing to track requests across regions, implementing chaos engineering to test region failures, optimizing costs with right-sizing instances and using spot instances for non-critical workloads, implementing auto-scaling per region based on local traffic, and using regional caching to reduce cross-region traffic.

title: Implement Event Sourcing for Financial System
question: Implement event sourcing for financial transaction system. Requirements: 1) Track all account transactions, 2) Full audit trail for compliance, 3) Ability to reconstruct account state at any point in time, 4) Handle high transaction volume (10K transactions per second), 5) Ensure no transaction loss, 6) Support for temporal queries (account balance at specific date). Discuss: using event sourcing pattern where all changes are stored as events in event store, designing immutable events (AccountCreated, MoneyDeposited, MoneyWithdrawn, AccountClosed) with event schema including timestamp, user, amount, reason, storing events in append-only event store (EventStoreDB, Kafka, or database table), using event versioning to handle schema changes, implementing aggregate pattern where Account is aggregate root that validates business rules, replaying events to rebuild current state of account, implementing snapshots for performance (store account state at intervals to avoid replaying all events), using CQRS to separate write model (event store) and read model (materialized views), projecting events to build read models in database or cache for fast queries, implementing event handlers that react to events (send notifications, update analytics), ensuring event ordering within aggregate using version numbers or sequence IDs, implementing idempotency to handle duplicate events, using distributed transaction pattern (saga) for operations spanning multiple aggregates, implementing event store partitioning by aggregate ID for scalability, using event replay for: fixing bugs (replay with fixed code), building new projections, migrating to new system, implementing temporal queries by replaying events up to specific timestamp, using event store for compliance and audit (immutable, complete history), implementing event archival for old events, and handling event store backup and disaster recovery.
